CHIEF COMPLAINT
Smoking cessation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old patient presenting with motivation to quit smoking. Smoking history began in high school with experimental use among friends and at parties, which progressed to daily use. Currently smokes 1.5 packs per day with first cigarette within 1 hour of waking. Denies use of other tobacco products. Patient previously attempted smoking cessation using cold turkey method, achieving approximately 1 year of abstinence before relapsing due to work-related stress from company downsizing and increased job responsibilities. Patient is currently highly motivated to quit smoking due to imminent fatherhood—daughter expected any day now. To address stress as a relapse trigger, patient has begun meditation practice and recently joined gym for stress management. Patient is willing to use pharmacologic aids for smoking cessation and has selected nicotine patch based on friends' positive experiences. Quit date set for next Monday, which is patient's birthday.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Nicotine Dependence
Patient is highly motivated to quit smoking. Quit date set for next Monday. Will initiate 21 mg transdermal nicotine patch on quit date. Instructed to change patch location daily to reduce/avoid skin irritation. Patch dose will be gradually decreased over time with adjustments made collaboratively. Provided with educational handouts regarding common smoking triggers. Counseled on importance of stress management given recent work stressors and upcoming major life changes with birth of daughter. Encouraged to continue exercise routine and consider meditation and/or yoga to support stress management efforts. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess progress and re-evaluate nicotine patch dosage.

2. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
Continue current management with diet and exercise. Hemoglobin A1c to be ordered for next blood draw. Results will be reviewed and discussed at follow-up visit in 2 weeks.

3. Gout
Continue allopurinol. Counseled to continue monitoring dietary factors that may exacerbate uric acid levels.
